dedupe_keys.name: pgrouting routing library for postgis and postgresql

description: pgRouting extends the PostGIS and PostgreSQL spatial database with routing functions, so that shortest paths, driving-distance areas and route optimisation run inside the database on network tables. The pgRouting Community maintains it; the project page lists Dijkstra and A* variants, bidirectional search, all-pairs shortest paths by Johnson and Floyd-Warshall, k-shortest paths, the travelling salesman problem, turn restriction paths and driving distance, and a workshop teaches its use. It is free and licensed under GPLv2. The GitHub releases page read on 2026-09-29 lists v4.0.2 of 5 September 2024 as the latest, so it counts as inactive under the two-year rule even though the project is widely used. Coverage is any network loaded by the user, most often OpenStreetMap roads, and no data are bundled. Caveats: it needs PostgreSQL and PostGIS administration and does not model traffic dynamics. It suits network flow analysis, accessibility and logistics routing for roads and other linear infrastructure. Related catalogue records: model-openrouteservice and model-opentripplanner.
